subject: biology
title: Plant hormones and tropisms
key_idea: (Separate science) Plants respond to light and gravity by growing towards or away from them. Auxin is unevenly distributed, so one side of a shoot or root elongates faster than the other, and the plant bends. Gibberellins and ethene control other processes.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Plant hormones control and coordinate growth. A tropism is a growth response to a stimulus.

items.meaning: A growth response of part of a plant to a stimulus.
A plant hormone that makes cells elongate.

items: Auxin is unevenly distributed in a shoot or root.
Auxin makes cells elongate, so the side where cells elongate faster grows more and the plant bends.
Other tropisms include hydrotropism (water), chemotropism (chemicals) and thermotropism (heat).
A tropism is a growth response to a stimulus.
Auxin is unevenly distributed, so growth is uneven and the plant bends.

blocks.text: Pick a situation to see where the auxin goes and how the plant responds.

diagram.alt: Pick a plant situation and see where the auxin collects and how the plant grows.

options.label: Shoot with light from one side
results: On the shaded side of the shoot
The shaded side, because auxin causes cell elongation there
The shoot bends towards the light (phototropism)

options.label: Shoot lying horizontal
results: On the lower side of the shoot
The lower side, because auxin causes cell elongation there
The shoot bends upwards, away from gravity

options.label: Root lying horizontal
results: On the lower side of the root
The upper side, because more auxin on the lower side means the lower side grows slower
The root bends downwards, in the direction of gravity

blocks.text: Why phototropism helps a plant survive

items: The leaves receive more light.
So there is more photosynthesis.
So the plant produces more glucose.
Put some seedlings in a box with a slit, so light comes from one direction.
Put others in the dark or in all-round light, as a control.
Measure the shoot heights at the start, then again after a suitable time. Use thread or straighten a bent shoot to measure it.
Use several seedlings and calculate the mean increase in height for each condition.
Keep temperature, volume of water, soil, age and species the same.
Shoots: auxin collects on the shaded side or lower side, so the shoot grows towards the light and upwards.
Roots: the upper side grows faster, so the root bends down.
Phototropism gives more light, photosynthesis and glucose.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Gibberellins and ethene control other processes. Their commercial uses are in the next note.

items: **Gibberellins** break seed dormancy, so seeds germinate. They also stimulate shoot elongation and flowering.
**Ethene** stimulates fruit ripening. It also causes the shedding of leaves.
Plant hormones also control flower opening.
Gibberellins: germination and shoot growth.
Ethene: fruit ripening and leaf shedding.

checks.q: Explain how phototropism is controlled in a plant shoot.
checks.a: Auxin moves to the shaded side of the shoot. It causes cell elongation there, so the shoot bends towards the light.

checks.q: A horizontal shoot bends upwards. Explain why, using auxin.
checks.a: Auxin collects on the lower side, so the lower side elongates faster and the shoot bends upwards, away from gravity.

checks.q: Describe one effect of gibberellins and one effect of ethene on plants.
checks.a: Gibberellins break seed dormancy (or elongate shoots). Ethene stimulates fruit ripening.

worked_example.question: Phototropism is a growth response by part of a plant to light. Explain how phototropism in a plant shoot helps the plant to survive.
answer_points: The leaves or plant receive or absorb more light (1).
So the plant produces more glucose (1).
worked_example.tip: Each step leads to the next. Starch, sugar or carbohydrate is accepted instead of glucose.

worked_example.question: Explain how phototropism is controlled in plant shoots.
answer_points: Phototropism is controlled by the hormone auxin (1).
Auxins move to the shaded side of the shoot (1).
This causes cell elongation, so the shoot bends towards the light (1).
worked_example.tip: Any three of the four points score. Name the hormone, say where it goes, and say what it does to the cells.

worked_example.question: A student investigates the effect of gravity on dandelion stems. The student places the equipment in a dark room. The dandelion stem is horizontal at the start of the investigation. During the investigation the stem moves upwards. Each hour the student measures the upward movement of the stem with a protractor. The upward movement is 0° at the start, then 10°, 27°, 45°, 59°, 74° and 90° after 1 to 6 hours. Describe and explain the results of this experiment. Use ideas about hormones.
answer_points: The dandelion stem bends or grows upwards (1).
The response is negatively gravitropic: the stem grows away from gravity (1).
Auxin gathers on, diffuses or passes to the lower side of the stem (1).
This causes more cell elongation on the lower side of the stem (1).
worked_example.tip: Describe the result first, then explain it with auxin.

worked_example.question:
Some maize seeds were pinned on a board and provided with light from all directions.

The board was placed in a clinostat that rotated the board. The board was rotated continuously as the seeds germinated and the roots grew. After 5 days the roots had grown horizontally.

Complete the sentences to explain the root growth.

Auxin is produced in shoot and root ______ . The auxin travels down the root by the process of ______ .
As the clinostat rotates, the effect of ______ on all sides of the root is equal.
This causes the distribution of auxin in the root to be ______ .
Auxin stimulates cell ______ causing the roots to grow horizontally.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each missing word.

items: (Supplement) Auxin is made in the tip of the shoot and in the tip of the root.
(Supplement) Auxin diffuses down the shoot from the tip.
(Supplement) If gravity or light acts equally on all sides, auxin is spread equally and the shoot or root grows straight.

worked_example.question:
The passage describes how plants respond to stimuli.

Complete the passage by writing a suitable word in each blank space.

Plant responses to directional stimuli are known as ______ .

Plant shoots respond to light coming from one direction by growing ______ the light. This is known as a positive ______ response. It is caused when a plant growth substance called ______ diffuses away from the light. This increases the rate of growth on the side of the shoot furthest away from the light.

Shoots also respond to ______ . This is known as a ______ geotropic response.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each correct word.

blocks.text: Tropisms are named by the direction of growth.

items: Growing towards the stimulus is a **positive** response. Growing away is a **negative** response.
Shoots are positively phototropic and negatively geotropic.
Roots are positively geotropic.
Auxin diffuses away from the light, so the shoot grows towards it.
